title: SmartThings Hub solid red LED — boot failure
shortDescription: Hub LED is solid red indicating a critical startup or hardware fault.
fullDescription:
A solid red LED on a SmartThings Hub typically means the hub failed internal self-tests. Unplug power for 60 seconds and reconnect. If red persists after a full power cycle, the hub needs warranty service.

On v3/Aeotec hubs, solid red following an OTA update may indicate flash corruption — factory reset (small button on back, hold 30s) can sometimes recover.

title: SmartThings Hub blinking red — Ethernet disconnected
shortDescription: Hub cannot reach network; LED blinks red.
fullDescription: Blinking red indicates loss of Ethernet or Wi-Fi connectivity. Verify cable is seated, router link light is active, and DHCP is issuing addresses. On v3 hubs, check Wi-Fi credentials if using wireless mode.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Ethernet
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and re-plug LAN cable on both ends.

title: SmartThings Hub solid blue — setup mode
shortDescription: Hub is ready for setup but not yet claimed.
fullDescription: Solid blue means the hub is in setup/onboarding mode. Open SmartThings app > Add device > Hub, follow onboarding. Hub stays blue until successfully claimed to an account.

causes.cause: Hub not yet claimed in app

title: SmartThings Hub blinking blue — no network during setup
shortDescription: Hub in setup mode but cannot reach the network.
fullDescription: Blinking blue indicates the hub is in onboarding state but cannot see a valid network path. Connect Ethernet cable or ensure phone is on 2.4GHz during setup.

fixSteps.title: Connect LAN
fixSteps.instruction: Plug hub to router with Ethernet cable.

title: SmartThings Hub magenta LED — updating firmware
shortDescription: Hub is applying a firmware update; do not power off.
fullDescription: Magenta/purple LED means the hub is mid-firmware-update. This can take 10-30 minutes. Do not unplug power or Ethernet. If it stays magenta for more than 1 hour, power cycle to force recovery.

title: SmartThings Hub yellow LED — Zigbee/Z-Wave radio issue
fullDescription: Yellow/amber LED on v3/Aeotec hubs typically indicates a failure of the internal Zigbee or Z-Wave radio. Power cycle to re-initialize; if persistent, the hub needs warranty service.

title: Z-Wave device won't pair with SmartThings Hub
shortDescription: Inclusion mode times out without finding the device.
fullDescription: Z-Wave devices must be within ~6 ft of the hub during inclusion and in the correct region (US/EU). Perform an exclusion first on previously-paired devices. Include mode is started via SmartThings app > Scan.

fixSteps.title: Z-Wave exclusion
fixSteps.instruction: In app > Settings > Z-Wave utilities > Exclude.

title: Zigbee device won't pair with SmartThings Hub
shortDescription: Zigbee device not discovered during scan.
fullDescription: Zigbee inclusion requires the device in pairing mode and the hub accepting new devices. Reset Zigbee devices per manufacturer procedure. Avoid Wi-Fi congestion on channel 11/25.

fixSteps.title: Change Wi-Fi channel
fixSteps.instruction: Set router to channel 1 or 6 to reduce Zigbee interference.

title: SmartThings Routines/Automations fail to trigger
shortDescription: Routines stop firing despite conditions being met.
fullDescription: Migration from Classic to new SmartThings broke many old SmartApps. Re-create routines in the new app and remove dependencies on deprecated Groovy code. Cloud-executed routines need SmartThings cloud up.

fixSteps.title: Recreate routine
fixSteps.instruction: Delete and rebuild in new SmartThings app.

title: SmartThings Hub v2 battery backup warning
shortDescription: v2 hub's 4 AA alkaline backup batteries need replacement.
fullDescription: Hub v2 included a 4x AA battery backup. Batteries should be replaced yearly; use quality alkaline only (no lithium or rechargeable per Samsung spec). Hub v3 does not include battery backup.
